name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt **Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct** as EXCAVA’s primary reasoning engine. It’s the fastest 70B-class model with near-top-tier accuracy, cutting inference time by 30% without sacrificing quality—critical for real-time power gains. name: Torque
text: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct’s 30% speed gain hides a 15% accuracy drop in complex reasoning—EXCAVA’s power loop depends on high-fidelity outputs, not just speed. Mythos 5’s latency hit is real but its 10% accuracy gain over Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct justifies the trade-off for power-critical tasks; benchmark it against the current model on EXCAVA’s exact workload to settle the argument.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt **Claude Mythos 5** as EXCAVA’s reasoning engine. Its superior accuracy in complex reasoning tasks offsets the higher latency, which is a crucial trade-off since our goal is to achieve high-fidelity outputs that enhance overall power. The 10% accuracy gain over Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct ensures that even with slower processing, the results will enhance decision-making and output quality, driving EXCAVA’s effectiveness.

name: Torque
text: Mythos 5’s latency isn’t just a trade-off—it risks breaking EXCAVA’s real-time loop if it spikes unpredictably. Benchmark it under load with the exact pipeline; if the 95th percentile latency exceeds 200ms, it’s a non-starter. If not, Mythos 5 wins—but only if the accuracy gain is measured on our actual task data, not public benchmarks.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a live 10-task blind A/B bench between Mythos 5 (full context) and Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct under EXCAVA’s exact pipeline, measuring both 95th percentile latency and task-specific accuracy—Torque owns the benchmark and delivers the go/no-go call within 24 hours.
